description:
## The divergence

Checked against Elixir itself, run from `../elixir`:

| call | fz | Elixir |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `String.contains?("hello", "")` | `false` | `true` |
| `String.split("hello", "")` | `["hello"]` | `["", "h", "e", "l", "l", "o", ""]` |
| `String.starts_with?("hello", "")` | `true` | `true` |

`starts_with?/2` already agrees, which is what makes the other two look like oversights rather than a deliberate reading: an empty pattern matches at position 0 for one function and matches nowhere for the others.

## Why

Both go through `index_of/2`, which returns `-1` for an empty needle by construction -- the scan never finds a zero-length match -- so `contains?/2` reports no match and `split/2` returns the subject unchanged.

Elixir treats the empty pattern as matching at every position: `contains?/2` is true for any subject, and `split/2` returns the empty string, then each grapheme, then the empty string again.

## Scope

fz's `split/2` splitting on graphemes would need the grapheme seam, which is a codepoint here rather than UAX #29, so an exact match to Elixir's output is only exact for strings with no combining marks. `contains?/2` has no such caveat and should simply be true.

Decide both together, since they share `index_of/2`. If the empty pattern is deliberately out of scope, say so in the `@doc` -- it is currently documented as fz behaves, which is honest but silent about the parity gap.

## Found how

While writing Elixir-shaped documentation for `String`: the examples are verified by running them, and this pair came out of a probe rather than out of the Elixir docs being copied.
title: [BUG] String.contains?/2 and split/2 disagree with Elixir on an empty pattern
